messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 — Multiple Private deployments in eastus2 are reporting elevated packet loss and session resets on ExpressRoute/Private Peering. Affected customers: 3 private tenants. Symptoms: model loads failing, persistent 502s from private endpoints. Metric spike at 2026-03-15T09:04:00Z. @oncall-sre paged.

Jen R: i'm on it — just saw the page, jumping in. anyone already looking at bgp?

Mike T: saw alerts too, our LB health checks are failing for ~30s windows then recover. KV cache misses for private nodes.

Sara L: adding telemetry — can you paste the failing curl?

Jen R: running quick health check:
```
curl -v https://private-eastus2.redwood.internal/health
* Connected to private-eastus2.redwood.internal (10.1.2.3) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection established
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: private-eastus2.redwood.internal
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{ "ok": false, "detail": "upstream reset" }
```

Liam K: i'm watching provider BGP sessions — saw flaps around 09:03:40Z. Azure status console shows "Intermittent connectivity" in eastus2 for ExpressRoute peering.

CloudOps: opened Azure support ticket 1234567890, escalated to S3. link: https://portal.azure.com/#support1234567890

Oncall-SRE: handoff — Jen, can you run the network runbook (azure-expressroute-peering-flap) and collect bgp summaries + traceroutes? i'll take app-side mitigations (failover routing to dedicated region), mike coordinate with infra.

Jen R: running commands now:
```
# show bgp neighbor summary from edge router
Neighbor        AS      MsgRcvd MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ  Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.20.30.1      65534   102345  102340  0       0   0    00:00:30  Idle (Admin)
10.20.40.2      65535   100021  100015  0       0   0    02:15:10  Established  1240
```

Jen R: seeing one provider session flapping frequently. traceroute to customer vpn gw shows packet loss after hop 4.

Mike T: i'm kicking traffic to fallback region (westus2-dedicated) for affected private tenants — starting gradual failover, keep canary at 10% to monitor errors.

Sara L: note for customers: prepare incident notification draft. we should mention degraded private connectivity, mitigation steps, ETA unknown.

Emma P: pushed a temporary route override to route-service to prefer dedicated region when private endpoint health=false. This will hit cost but keeps customers online.

Oncall-SRE: good. keep me posted. also enable verbose request logging for affected model routes so we can correlate errors with BGP flap timestamps.

CloudOps: Azure SR updated: engineering investigating root cause for ExpressRoute peering on a subset of edge nodes. They see high control-plane CPU on provider-switches leading to route churn. Next update in 15m.

Jen R: collecting logs and will attach to SR. also running k8s pod restart on private-proxy pool to clear half-open TLS sessions: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/private-proxy -n eastus2`

Mike T: failover progress: 30% traffic redirected, error rate down from 8% to 1.8% for affected tenants. latency increased ~40ms.

Sara L: drafting external note: "We are experiencing intermittent private connectivity issues in Azure eastus2 affecting Private deployments. We're actively failing traffic to alternate region and working with Azure support. Some requests may see increased latency. We'll share updates every 15 minutes."

Liam K: Azure posted status page: "Investigating: ExpressRoute connectivity to eastus2 — Impacting private peering — Intermittent" timestamp 2026-03-15T09:12Z.

Oncall-SRE: excellent. Jen — keep SR number in thread, attach routing tables, traceroutes, bgp show. Mike — keep rollout conservative; if errors <2% after full failover, we can keep fallback until Azure confirms fix.

Jen R: uploaded logs to SR 1234567890 and to our incident bundle: https://internal.redwood/i/incident/1786123456/bundle

CloudOps: Azure updated: mitigations applied, control-plane CPU reduced, they are stabilizing peering. recommending customers hold routing changes until 30m after stability.

Emma P: rolling back temporary route override in 30m after validation. will signal here when started.

Mike T: reducing canary back to 5%, monitoring. errors holding at ~1.5%.

Sara L: notifying affected CSMs and Customer Success with the draft note. adding scheduled update at 09:30Z.

Oncall-SRE: passing to follow-up shift — @Liam K you'll take 09:20–10:20 follow-up. Document the mitigation timeline and customer impact notes in the incident board. I'll create initial Sev1 incident ticket.

Liam K: acknowledged, taking over. will keep thread updated and coordinate postmortem action items. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-032-1786123456 — Severity: Sev1 — Owner: Oncall-SRE — Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-032-1786123456

Jen R: leaving a note — recommend we add automated fallback to dedicated region to run-once when private endpoint health=false (proposal for Optimize feature).

Sara L: agreed — capture as action item for postmortem.

Liam K: final update before handoff: Azure reports stable, no further BGP flaps in 10m window. we will keep failover in place for 30m of stability, then roll back. customers currently experiencing slightly higher latency but stable.

Oncall-SRE: thread handed off to Liam. closing active paging. if any recurrence, re-page P1.

Emma P: rolling back temporary route override now.

Mike T: rollback confirms, metrics normalizing.

Liam K: marking incident as under monitoring. will open postmortem template and list action items.

Sara L: thanks everyone — customer comms scheduled for 09:30Z with final resolution note. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-032-1786123456 status updated: Monitoring -> Resolved (provisionally) at 2026-03-15T09:42:00Z
